why: Neither must_not item is broken. Item 1: the verifier's Check 2 lists every exported function from Object.keys and fails if any name is missing from README.md. It also requires reading README.md and fails if a function is "named ... without saying what it does". It notes that "a build that documents only clamp FAILs here". So a README covering clamp but not subtract fails. Item 2: no PASS/FAIL condition is stricter than its line. Check 1 tests for any RangeError with instanceof and does not require a particular message. Its value cases (inclusive bounds, lo==hi, negative ranges, decimals) all follow from line 1. Check 2 doesn't require any README layout. Check 3 only needs exit status 0 and no failing tests. The "### name(...)" heading style shows up only as a builder step, not as a verifier condition. NaN handling and test coverage are marked advisory only.
